Let \(r\) be the number of red segments and \(b\) the number of blue segments.  
Each color forms a simple closed polygonal chain, so the red chain has \(r\) sides and the blue chain has \(b\) sides. Hence
\[
r\le N,\qquad b\le N.
\]
Since every segment is colored exactly once,
\[
r+b=\binom N2.
\]
Thus
\[
\binom N2 \le 2N \implies \frac{N(N-1)}2\le 2N \implies N\le 5.
\]
Also a closed chain needs at least \(3\) sides, so \(N\ge 3\).

- \(N=3\): \(\binom32=3\), but \(r,b\ge 3\), impossible.
- \(N=4\): \(r+b=6\), so \(r=b=3\). Two triangles would partition \(K_4\), but any two triangles in \(K_4\) share an edge, impossible.
- \(N=5\): possible. For example take
\[
A=(0,0),\ B=(1,0),\ C=(0,1),\ D=(0.2,0.1),\ E=(0.1,0.2).
\]
Use the red cycle
\[
A-D-E-B-C-A
\]
and the blue cycle
\[
A-B-D-C-E-A.
\]
These partition all \(10\) edges of \(K_5\), and each cycle is non-self-intersecting.

Therefore the only possible value is
\[
\boxed{5}.
\]
